rule: ruling:sam-2026-10-07 claims 9 and 10 (ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-009, -p1-010): a DR1 judgement on the same difference, or a real persistence constraint the prototype cannot express, overrides the prototype; how records saved before roles existed are filtered is exactly such a persistence constraint (the prototype has no untyped records), and DR1 row inc-048 (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-051) already judged it: until a record carries a type, filtering it on a guess would hide addresses the trader legitimately wants, so an untyped record is not hidden.
outcome: Each party picker filters typed address-book records by its role, as Design Release 2.1 does (prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-063); an existing record with no role yet is offered on every party picker until it is given one, in the compose stack and in CDP alike, because DR1's inc-048 judgement (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-051) rules out hiding addresses the trader legitimately wants on a guess, and records saved before roles existed are a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express. The stub-mode records are each given roles so stub mode shows the filtering.
